name: InboxAlly
summary: Email deliverability tool that trains your sender reputation: engagement-based signals keep your campaigns and cold outreach out of spam and in the primary inbox. Works alongside any ESP or email platform.
best_for: serious senders (email marketers and cold-outreach teams) whose deliverability problems are costing measurable revenue and who need active reputation repair
skip_if: you're a small sender who just needs basic list hygiene (cheaper warm-up tools suffice), or your inbox issues stem from content and list quality you haven't fixed
honest_knock: This is a premium, seed-list-based deliverability tool, and the price reflects it: Starter alone is well above casual warm-up apps, so it only makes sense if inbox placement is costing you real revenue. It improves sender reputation through engagement signals, but it's not a magic fix for bad content or a purchased list: deliverability still depends on how you actually send. Buy it when the math (lost revenue from spam-foldering) clearly beats the monthly fee.

pricing.entry_price_terms: per month (100 seed emails/day, 1 sender profile)
pricing.notes: (price re-verified 2026-08-31 against the vendor's own pricing page, read from a European exit, and unchanged on 2026-09-29 and 2026-10-14) Every amount unchanged and confirmed on the plan comparison table, which states 'Pricing in USD, billed monthly': Starter $149/mo (100 seed emails/day, 1 sender profile), Plus $645/mo (500/day, 5 profiles), Premium $1,190/mo (1,000/day, 10 profiles), Enterprise custom (custom volume, unlimited profiles, dedicated deliverability experts). 10-day free trial, no card. No annual billing option is offered. Premium's sessions, more precisely than the previous dossier: a 1-hour setup/strategy session plus weekly 30-minute progress reviews. VENDOR SELF-CONTRADICTION, confirm before relying: the tier cards give Starter 'Email support' and reserve live chat for Plus and above, while the comparison table lower on the same page ticks 'Live chat support' and 'Dedicated CSM' for all four tiers including Starter. Phone & Zoom support, the setup session and the weekly reviews are consistently Premium-and-above in both places. Every plan includes IA Score, IA Reputation, Adaptive Autowarmup, the in-app IA Assistant, the full REST API, native CRM integrations and inbox placement testing. Re-read 2026-09-29: the page's own FAQ now goes further than either, saying email, live chat, phone and Zoom support are 'all standard' and a dedicated CSM is assigned on every plan, while the cards and the table still keep Phone & Zoom for Premium and above. The same FAQ says full reputation repair typically takes 4 to 8 weeks, so the 10-day trial is for judging fit rather than completing a warm-up.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session used two free tools of InboxAlly without an account. The Spam Word Checker counted 23 spam words in our made-up cold mail after one paste, with the result on screen at once, and the DKIM Checker found 9 records for mailchimp.com (6 healthy, 3 needs attention) in 0.3s. The prices on the pricing page are the same as in the dossier (Starter $149, Plus $645, Premium $1,190 a month billed monthly, Enterprise on request) and the page promises a 10-day free trial with no credit card. The sign-up was not opened and nothing was bought, so the trial, the warm-up itself and the cancelling were not tested. Account and start: no account was used. Our AI assistant ran the test in a tab of our Chrome on the free tools of InboxAlly (inboxally.com/free-tools), which need no login (the interface is in English; a cookie banner appeared and was not clicked, and the tools worked anyway). The dossier name is InboxAlly and the review is on MSS (mss/inboxally-review.html). The audience from the dossier: cold-outreach teams with one damaged domain. The test date is 18 Nov 2026; the start time was not recorded in the notes. Start: the page heading says FREE and NO SIGNUP REQUIRED, and the FAQ answers the question whether you need an account with No. Every tool works instantly without signup or login. Run 1, Spam Word Checker (/email-content-tester/): the tool was prefilled with a sample text of 11 words, which we replaced with the subject FREE offer: act now, limited time!!! and our own cold mail full of trigger phrases (guaranteed 100% free cash bonus, Click here, risk-free prize, Act now, urgent, Buy now!). It is a live scan with no button and no account: one paste and the result was on screen. The counter showed 23 Spam Words and the list Possible Spam Trigger Words: free, offer, act, now, limited, congratulations, guaranteed, 100% free, cash, bonus, click, here, risk-free, prize, urgent, expires today, earn, money, fast, buy and %. Our text was written to trigger the filter, so the number says what the tool does and nothing about the quality of a real mail. Run 2, DKIM Checker (/dkim-checker/) on the public domain mailchimp.com, without a selector: the page showed 9 DKIM records discovered, 6 healthy, 3 needs attention, completed in 0.3s. The tester wrote down k2, k3, mte1, mte2 and zendesk1 and zendesk2 as healthy and google (RSA 1024) and k1 (RSA 1024) as needs attention, so only eight of the nine records were named in the notes. The page adds that a published key does not prove your mail is being signed. Page count: the tester reported that the free tools page speaks of ten diagnostic utilities but shows 11 cards; this is a report from the session summary and is not in the raw notes. Plans: inboxally.com pricing page, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in US dollars, billed monthly (the page line is USD, billed monthly): Starter $149/mo (100 seed mails a day, 1 sender profile), Plus $645/mo (500 a day, 5 sender profiles), Premium $1,190/mo (1,000 a day, 10 sender profiles, phone calls, a setup session of 1 hour and weekly reviews of half an hour) and Enterprise on request (Contact us). The page says Try now free for 10 days, no credit card required. All amounts are the same as in the dossier (read 14 Oct 2026), so the price is UNCHANGED. The trial was not started; the sign-up sits behind the button Try Free and was not opened. The pricing FAQ gives Starter email help only, while a line on the same page says that live chat and a customer success manager come with every plan, as the dossier already noted; nobody was contacted, so which is true was not tested. Cancelling: not applicable, there is no account. Not tested: the paid warm-up, the free trial, an account, cancelling, the Email Spam Checker (it sends a real mail), List Verification and the Placement Tester. Clean up: no account and no test data; the own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free tools say little about the paid product: a spam word count of a mail we wrote to trigger the filter, and a DKIM list for a public domain. The page sets two lines on live chat and a customer success manager against an email only line for Starter. The tester reports that the free tools page speaks of ten utilities and shows 11 cards.

exit_test.what: No account was needed; the tool ran without signing in. On 18 November 2026 the session used two free tools of InboxAlly without an account. The Spam Word Checker counted 23 spam words in our made-up cold mail after one paste, with the result on screen at once, and the DKIM Checker found 9 records for mailchimp.com (6 healthy, 3 needs attention) in 0.3s. The prices on the pricing page are the same as in the dossier (Starter $149, Plus $645, Premium $1,190 a month billed monthly, Enterprise on request) and the page promises a 10-day free trial with no credit card. The sign-up was not opened and nothing was bought, so the trial, the warm-up itself and the cancelling were not tested. Account and start: no account was used. Our AI assistant ran the test in a tab of our Chrome on the free tools of InboxAlly (inboxally.com/free-tools), which need no login (the interface is in English; a cookie banner appeared and was not clicked, and the tools worked anyway). The dossier name is InboxAlly and the review is on MSS (mss/inboxally-review.html). The audience from the dossier: cold-outreach teams with one damaged domain. The test date is 18 Nov 2026; the start time was not recorded in the notes. Start: the page heading says FREE and NO SIGNUP REQUIRED, and the FAQ answers the question whether you need an account with No. Every tool works instantly without signup or login. Run 1, Spam Word Checker (/email-content-tester/): the tool was prefilled with a sample text of 11 words, which we replaced with the subject FREE offer: act now, limited time!!! and our own cold mail full of trigger phrases (guaranteed 100% free cash bonus, Click here, risk-free prize, Act now, urgent, Buy now!). It is a live scan with no button and no account: one paste and the result was on screen. The counter showed 23 Spam Words and the list Possible Spam Trigger Words: free, offer, act, now, limited, congratulations, guaranteed, 100% free, cash, bonus, click, here, risk-free, prize, urgent, expires today, earn, money, fast, buy and %. Our text was written to trigger the filter, so the number says what the tool does and nothing about the quality of a real mail. Run 2, DKIM Checker (/dkim-checker/) on the public domain mailchimp.com, without a selector: the page showed 9 DKIM records discovered, 6 healthy, 3 needs attention, completed in 0.3s. The tester wrote down k2, k3, mte1, mte2 and zendesk1 and zendesk2 as healthy and google (RSA 1024) and k1 (RSA 1024) as needs attention, so only eight of the nine records were named in the notes. The page adds that a published key does not prove your mail is being signed. Page count: the tester reported that the free tools page speaks of ten diagnostic utilities but shows 11 cards; this is a report from the session summary and is not in the raw notes. Plans: inboxally.com pricing page, read by the tester on 18 Nov 2026 in US dollars, billed monthly (the page line is USD, billed monthly): Starter $149/mo (100 seed mails a day, 1 sender profile), Plus $645/mo (500 a day, 5 sender profiles), Premium $1,190/mo (1,000 a day, 10 sender profiles, phone calls, a setup session of 1 hour and weekly reviews of half an hour) and Enterprise on request (Contact us). The page says Try now free for 10 days, no credit card required. All amounts are the same as in the dossier (read 14 Oct 2026), so the price is UNCHANGED. The trial was not started; the sign-up sits behind the button Try Free and was not opened. The pricing FAQ gives Starter email help only, while a line on the same page says that live chat and a customer success manager come with every plan, as the dossier already noted; nobody was contacted, so which is true was not tested. Cancelling: not applicable, there is no account. Not tested: the paid warm-up, the free trial, an account, cancelling, the Email Spam Checker (it sends a real mail), List Verification and the Placement Tester. Clean up: no account and no test data; the own tab was closed. No kit records were entered.
exit_test.awkward: The free tools say little about the paid product: a spam word count of a mail we wrote to trigger the filter, and a DKIM list for a public domain. The page sets two lines on live chat and a customer success manager against an email only line for Starter. The tester reports that the free tools page speaks of ten utilities and shows 11 cards.
